In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the adsorption behavior of volatile components on hydrophobically modified resins can be described with multi-component adsorption models, and that the optimal resins for selective adsorption are Sepabeads and Amberlite resin series.
Sepabeads and Amberlite resins are the most suitable adsorbents for selective removal of flavor-active components from water/ ethanol mixtures.

XAD16N is the best resin to be used for selective adsorption and removal of flavor-active compounds from ethanol/water solutions, while Sepabeads are the best resins for removal of ethanol from water.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
a resin can be chosen based on its selectivity over ethanol for selective adsorption or selective removal of flavor-active components.
the adsorption of flavor components is strongly influenced by the resin type, and the adsorption of ethanol is the most challenging process.

the proposed resin selection method is applicable and useful in industrial practice, and the results can be applied for the selection of resins for selective adsorption and removal of flavor-active components from alcoholic beverages.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the miniaturized batch method is suitable for screening of hydrophobic adsorbents for selective removal of flavor-active compounds from aqueous mixtures.

the miniaturized batch adsorption technique can be used for screening adsorbents for selective removal of flavor-active components from water/ ethanol mixtures and the proposed multi-component adsorption models can be used for describing adsorption behavior of the tested resins in multi-component adsorption systems.
the adsorption of flavor components on synthetic hydrophobics is highly selective and can be used to tune flavor of alcoholic beverage.
